grants.Program Focus:
OPENING SUMMARY — WEEK OF OCTOBER 26 – 30, 2026

Week at a Glance:

A light week on the federal side: 27 Grants.gov postings between October 23 and 29, eleven of them with a GMA client path, plus the opening of the FY2027 DoD SBIR/STTR Release 1 and a $5 billion USDA loan-guarantee program for meat, poultry and seafood processing. The largest new item landed on Friday October 30, after the window closed: DOE's $237 million Grid SCALED cooperative-agreement opportunity for domestic grid-component manufacturing, with concept papers due November 20. Themes: forest and landscape restoration (Forest Service LSR and its tribal set-aside, both due January 26), defense basic research (two AFOSR solicitations, one with a November 18 pre-proposal date), and financing over grants (SPUR guarantees; two multibillion-dollar DOE Energy Dominance Financing actions). California opened its $27.5 million LWCF local cycle, released the HOMES pay-for-performance implementer RFP and started the Prop 4 land-repurposing guidelines; Texas TERP has a first-come port program open and a public-fleet round coming in December. Policy was dominated by Section 232 actions, a proposed tribal Build America, Buy America waiver extension (comments November 23) and a proposed rewrite of the HHS block-grant rules (comments November 30).

Grid Supply Chain Manufacturing:

DOE Office of Electricity / NETL Grid Supply Chain Alternatives to Lead Energy Dominance (Grid SCALED, DE-FOA-0003641) — $237,000,000 in cooperative agreements, about 70 awards: up to $50,000,000 for refurbishment and reuse of existing grid equipment and up to $187,000,000 for U.S.-sourced alternative materials and subcomponents. Grants.gov lists eligibility as unrestricted and cost share as required (percentage in the NOFO, which did not render). Concept papers due November 20, 2026 to qualify for a full application; full applications February 8, 2027. First notice under DOE's $375 million Grid Supply Chain Program; solid-state transformer funding expected in 2027.

DOE SBIR/STTR — Fall 2026 Phase I:

DOE Office of Technology Commercialization Fall 2026 (FY26 Fall) SBIR/STTR Phase I — the first full cycle under the restructured pitch-first program run through the ConnectWerx hub: 25 topics across EERE successor offices, CESER, HGEO, Nuclear Energy, Office of Electricity, Office of Science and NNSA (critical minerals, manufacturing scale-up, batteries, grid innovation, cybersecurity, nuclear, fusion, detectors, proliferation and detonation detection). Hub page: about 160 awards, up to $50,000,000 in Phase I, up to $300,000 per award ($306,500 with TABA), Fast-Track with Phase II at a go/no-go; DOE's release says "more than $200 million" across phases. Up to three pitches per company. Pitches due December 16, 2026, 2:00 p.m. ET via the AMP portal; office hours November 19 and December 1.

Forest and Landscape Restoration:

USDA Forest Service Landscape Scale Restoration (USDA-FS-2026-LSR) — $11,340,000, $100,000–$300,000 per project ($600,000 multistate), 1:1 match, states, local governments, tribes, nonprofits and universities; every non-tribal applicant needs State Forester sponsorship, with drafts due to the State Forester (CAL FIRE in California) by December 17; applications due January 26, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET. A companion tribal notice (USDA-FS-2026-LSR-TRIBAL, $100,000–$300,000, emailed application, same deadline) needs no sponsor.

Climate, Coastal and Hazard Science:

NOAA Climate Program Office FY2027 AI and machine-learning competition (NOAA-OAR-CPO-2027-33392) — up to $250,000 per year for up to 15 awards to universities, nonprofits, companies and local or tribal governments; LOIs encouraged by November 17, applications due February 9, 2027, 11:59 p.m. PT; foreign institutions and state governments are not listed as eligible. NOAA National Ocean Service FY2026–2028 BAA (NOAA-NOS-MB-2027-33927) is open to September 30, 2028 but carries no appropriated funds; CESU partner institutions have the cleanest path.

Transportation Safety:

FMCSA FY2027 Crash Causal Factors Program (FM-CCFP-27-001) — $7,000,000, up to $500,000 per award, no match, cooperative agreements to state and local law enforcement collecting fatal heavy-truck crash data. Only the 30 Heavy-Duty Truck Study sample states and named local agencies are eligible; California is not a participating state (Texas, Arizona, Nevada and Washington are). Due December 28, 2026, 5:00 p.m. ET.

Justice:

BJA FY2026 Postconviction Testing of DNA Evidence (O-BJA-2026-172771) — up to $11,179,802, up to $1,000,000 per award, 14 awards, to states, local governments and public universities. Chief-executive certification (Appendix 1) required for state and local applicants. Grants.gov December 8; JustGrants December 15, 2026, 8:59 p.m. ET.

Defense Research and SBIR:

AFOSR University Center for High-Speed Aerothermoelasticity (FA955027S0001) — one award, $2,750,000 per year for up to five years ($13,750,000), U.S. universities only, $750,000 per year of it contingent on three HBCU investigators; white papers required January 22, 2027, full proposals April 2, 2027. AFOSR–Taiwan NSTC Frontiers in Materials (FA955027S0002) — about eight pairs at $150,000 per year per U.S. PI; pre-proposals due November 18, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET and each must name a Taiwan co-investigator. DoD SBIR/STTR FY2027 Release 1 opened October 28 and closes November 25 (25 topics; Air Force Direct-to-Phase-II awards up to $2,000,000).

Gulf Coast Restoration (restricted pool):

Treasury RESTORE Act Direct Component Non-Construction (GR-RDC-26-002) and Centers of Excellence (GR-RCE-26-001) — allocation-based, rolling to October 31, 2027, no match. Only the designated Gulf state entities, Florida counties and Louisiana parishes may apply; Texas and Gulf university clients reach the Centers of Excellence money through state subaward competitions.

School Nutrition Equipment:

USDA FNS Harvest to Hallways NSLP Equipment Assistance Grants (USDA-FNA-CN-HTH-NSLP-EAG-2027) — $50,000,000 by formula to the 54 state agencies (California $5,554,836), due January 11, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET; state agencies only — school districts and county offices of education compete for subgrants from their state in 2027.

Agricultural Processing Finance:

USDA SPUR Guaranteed Loan Program FY2027 (91 FR 67540) — at least $5,000,000,000 in loan level, 90% guarantees up to $175,000,000 per borrower, terms to 40 years, for meat, poultry and seafood processing by companies, cooperatives, nonprofits, tribes and public bodies; nationally dominant beef, pork and poultry processors excluded. Rolling from October 23 (NOFO) or October 27 (Federal Register) until funds run out.

Research and Education:

NSF 27-011 Dear Colleague Letter — supplements of up to $100,000 per PI for existing EDU and ExLENT awardees only, requests due November 10, 2026, for Presidential SI Challenge activities. NIH Kids First U24s (RFA-RM-27-008, $3,500,000 direct costs per year; RFA-RM-27-010, $900,000) due January 8, 2027, domestic institutions only; NIBIB NextTech R18 (RFA-EB-28-004, $6,000,000 for 8–12 awards, direct costs rarely above $750,000 per year, for-profits eligible) first due February 1, 2027.

California:

State Parks LWCF 2027 local cycle (Portal 194175) — $27,500,000, up to $6,000,000 per applicant, 50% match, cities, counties, tribes and park districts, due January 14, 2027, 11:59 p.m.. CEC RFP-26-501 HOMES Pay-for-Performance Statewide Implementer — one contract to run more than $90,000,000 in rebates; pre-bid November 10, questions November 16, proposals January 22, 2027. CDFW Mojave Desert Tortoise Recovery (Portal 193758) — $2,000,000, no match, six desert counties, workshop November 9, due December 3, 2026 (not previously covered). Department of Conservation Multibenefit Land Repurposing Prop 4 draft guidelines — $200,000,000, comments due December 7, first round projected winter 2026–27.

Texas:

TCEQ TERP SPRY — up to 80% of drayage-truck and cargo-handling replacement costs at Texas seaports and rail yards, first-come through March 12, 2027, 5:00 p.m. CT (not previously covered). TERP Governmental Alternative Fuel Fleet (GAFF) — public fleets over 15 vehicles, per-vehicle caps $17,000–$80,000, applications expected to open December 2026 (forecast).

Policy & Compliance Updates:

Eight agencies propose extending the tribal BABA manufactured-products waiver through December 31, 2026 (91 FR 66871; comments November 23). HHS proposes stripping substantive provisions from the block-grant rules at 45 CFR 96 (91 FR 68097; comments November 30). A Section 232 proclamation on robotics and industrial machinery (October 28) imposes no tariff but starts a 180-day negotiation clock, as did last week's wind-turbine proclamation (now 91 FR 68001). NRC finalized a rule letting reactor applicants rely on DOE or Department of War demonstration authorizations (effective November 25); DOE added helium to its Critical Material List; EPA proposed Alaska Class VI primacy (comments December 14) and a further rollback of the oil and gas methane rules (comments December 16). OMB/OPM rescinded the 2025 shutdown RIF guidance (M-27-01) ahead of the December 11 CR expiration; BLM terminated the Section 368 energy-corridor EIS; DOE's Energy Dominance Financing office announced a $5 billion nuclear-uprate commitment and closed a $5.1 billion utility loan; EPA launched its PFAS TECH research strategy and $26 million in school lead-reduction allotments.

Watch List / Upcoming:

Federal Register citations are now published for three items covered last week: Proclamation 11074 on wind turbines (91 FR 68001), EO 14438 Decreasing Housing Costs (91 FR 68007; the Manufactured Housing Task Force must report by about April 20, 2027 on whether federal grant funds can be conditioned on state and local permitting reform) and Presidential Determination 2027-01 on petroleum logistics under DPA Title III (91 FR 68011). DARPA: Proposers Day for the Nassau critical-infrastructure resilience program (IPTO) is December 10, 2026 in Arlington, registration due November 7, 2026, 5:00 p.m. ET (DARPA-SN-27-08; utilities and universities should register as teaming prospects); RFI DARPA-SS-27-01 on solid-state heat-to-electricity conversion closes November 23; Special Notice DARPA-SN-27-14 on utility-scale quantum-computing workshops takes responses to December 30. Expected within 30–90 days: EPA FY2027 Brownfields Assessment, RLF and Cleanup NOFOs are still "fall 2026" with nothing posted as of October 30 (no Multipurpose round in FY27; applications due about 60 days after posting; 20% cost share for Cleanup and RLF; prior Assessment grantees needed 70% drawdown by October 1); EPA Clean School Bus promises "additional information later in 2026" (page updated October 26); SERDP/ESTCP FY2028 BAAs (none posted; prior years released October–January); NASA ROSES-27 by January 2027 (about 50 elements, no ROSES-26) and OSTEM's planned Next Gen STEM TEAM II ($4.0 million) and EPSCoR Rapid Response ($2.6 million) NOFOs in FY27 Q1; the DOE AFFO NOFO (NOI DE-FOA-0003648, expected November); CARB CORE FY 2026-27 (calendar shows opens December 1, closes March 1, 2027); DOT FY2027 BUILD (calendar row added October 29 from a newsletter forecast — no DOT statement found); Texas Clean Fleet Program (TCEQ projects January 2027). NSF MRI still has no FY2027 solicitation. Deadline cluster, next three weeks: NSF 26-510/26-511 SBIR/STTR, NSF 26-513 AI Infrastructure Hubs and 26-512 AI Datasets November 4; CEC DEBA workshop November 5 and questions November 13; DURIP November 6; NRCS California batching November 6; Nassau registration November 7; NSF 27-011 and NMTC CY2026 November 10; USGS 104(g) November 12; USGS CESU agreements November 14; FEMA C-UAS and ONR Communications and Networking November 16; NTIA TBCP and NEGP November 17; NOAA CPO LOIs November 17; CTC SB 1 programs November 18–20; FCC NEPA comments and ETIPP November 18; NASA B.7 Step-1, ARPA-E UNLOCK concept papers and RUS ARC LOIs November 20; tribal BABA waiver comments November 23; DoD SBIR Release 1 November 25; HHS block-grant comments November 30. Awards and signals: USDA MPPEP $57.4 million (147 awards) and RCPP $325 million (42 projects) on October 26; MARAD PIDP $498 million to 35 ports on October 27 (debrief unsuccessful applicants); Commerce CHIPS R&D letters of intent totaling $389 million to four firms with a government minority equity stake as an award condition (October 22), a model advanced-manufacturing clients should understand; a Forest Service PRA notice for Wood Products Infrastructure Assistance (comments November 27) signals continued rounds; USDA Distance Learning and Telemedicine is still not accepting applications. ACL forecasts posted October 26–27: UCEDD core funding (HHS-2027-ACL-AOD-DDUC-0001, $26.4 million, 42 awards, est. post December 1, due February 1, 2027, existing UCEDD grantees only); Strengthening the Direct Care Workforce technical-assistance center (HHS-2027-ACL-AOD-DNDP-0016, one $2,000,000 cooperative agreement, est. post March 14, 2027, open to states, local governments, tribes, universities and nonprofits); National Center for Law and Elder Rights (HHS-2027-ACL-AOA-LMRC-0019, $1,500,000, four awards, est. post January 5, 2027, national nonprofits). California: CEC GFO-26-503 DEBA shows no addendum and its award range, eligibility and match remain only in the .docx manual (workshop November 5, 1:00–4:00 p.m.); DWR Dam Safety and Climate Resilience ($228.2 million; 50% match) is still a forecast although the portal said "anticipated opening October 2026"; CalRecycle Farm and Ranch Solid Waste Cleanup FR93 (Portal 163104; cities, counties, RCDs and tribes; LOI required; up to $200,000 per applicant; due January 6, 2027) was never profiled; SWRCB 319(h) 2027 is due December 18; GFO-26-601 Charger Service Skills Accelerator closed October 30. Texas: the THIVE page still says applications were expected "September 2026" while the TERP landing page lists THIVE as open — confirm with TERP before advising fleets. Inconsistencies to confirm: FA955027S0001's "$150,000 annually" budget line versus $2,750,000 per year elsewhere in the NOFO; LSR Tribal match (fact sheet 1:1, listing "No"); RFA-EB-28-004 close date (listing December 1, 2030 vs. announcement February 2, 2030); SPUR's open date (October 23 vs. 27) and a fee schedule dated "October 1, 2027"; Treasury's 26-series RESTORE FOA texts not yet posted (eligibility taken from the 25-series FOAs). The continuing resolution expires December 11, 2026 and OMB's 2 CFR 200 rewrite stays blocked until then; IRB 2026-44 carried no energy-credit guidance. Empower Innovation pages did not render this week — check its October newsletter manually; no Open Grant daily limit was hit, and its sweep surfaced nothing new beyond items already in the calendar.

grants.Opportunity #: DE-FOA-0003641 (ALN 81.122, Electricity Research, Development and Analysis)
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Electricity, administered by the National Energy Technology Laboratory. Grants.gov contact Alissa Temperine, NETL, 412-386-9661, alissa.temperine@netl.doe.gov. Technical and NOFO contacts: Not specified – needs verification at source (NOFO Part 2 did not render).
grants.Total Funding: $237,000,000; about 70 awards expected (Grants.gov). DOE's release: up to $50,000,000 for projects that refurbish and reuse existing grid equipment and materials, and up to $187,000,000 for projects that increase the use of alternative materials and subcomponents sourced and made in the U.S. First funding notice under DOE's Grid Supply Chain Program, which DOE says can provide up to $375 million; additional notices, including solid-state transformers, are expected in 2027.
grants.Award Range: Not specified – needs verification at source (the Grants.gov listing shows a $1 floor and a $237,000,000 ceiling, which are placeholders; per-topic award sizes are in NOFO Part 2, which did not render in our tools).
grants.Eligible Applicants: Grants.gov lists eligibility as "Unrestricted"; restrictions on foreign entities, national laboratories and FFRDCs, and any domestic-content or FEOC conditions are in the NOFO and need verification before outreach. Expected applicants: transformer and grid-component manufacturers, utilities and cooperatives with refurbishment programs, materials suppliers, and universities or national labs as team members.
grants.Deadline: Concept papers due November 20, 2026 (required to qualify for a full application; time and time zone not stated in the release — confirm in eXCHANGE); full applications February 8, 2027 (Grants.gov close date; time not listed); archive date March 10, 2027.
grants.Program Focus: DOE's first grid supply-chain manufacturing solicitation: cooperative agreements to expand domestic production and refurbishment of transformers and other critical grid components, substitute U.S.-sourced materials and subcomponents for imports, and cut utility equipment costs and lead times (DOE projects $125 million a year in utility savings). It fits manufacturing and advanced-materials companies, public power and cooperative utilities with equipment refurbishment or spares programs, and the universities and labs that partner with them; it also pairs with the DOE Grid Resilience formula money states and tribes are now applying for. Three weeks to a mandatory concept paper means outreach to manufacturing and utility clients should go out immediately, with eXCHANGE registration and teaming decisions in the first week of November. Good material for a focused campaign to grid-equipment manufacturers and utility supply-chain managers.
grants.Cost Share / Match: Cost sharing required (Grants.gov); percentage by topic or TRL Not specified – needs verification at source (NOFO Part 2). DOE typically requires 20% for R&D and 50% for demonstration and deployment under EPAct 2005 section 988.

grants.Description: USDA Forest Service — Landscape Scale Restoration Grant Program for Non-Federal Lands, FY2026
grants.Agency / Funder: USDA Forest Service, State, Private and Tribal Forestry. National inbox SM.FS.LSR@usda.gov; regional leads: California, Hawaii and Pacific Islands Jeremy Gooding, jeremy.gooding@usda.gov; Arizona and New Mexico Kathleen Moore, kathleen.moore@usda.gov; Oregon, Washington and Alaska Karl Dalla Rosa, karl.dallarosa@usda.gov; Idaho, Nevada, Utah, Montana and North Dakota Patrick Bridegam, patrick.a.bridegam@usda.gov.
grants.Total Funding: $11,340,000 under this NOFO (of $12.6 million appropriated program-wide); the NOFO estimates 20–40 awards (the listing shows 30).
grants.Award Range: $100,000 minimum; $300,000 maximum for single-state projects and $600,000 for multistate projects ($50,000 minimum in the territories); any one state or tribe is capped at 15% of its regional set-aside. Three-year performance period, extendable to five.
grants.Eligible Applicants: State forestry agencies, units of local government, federally recognized tribes, Alaska Native Corporations, Native Hawaiian Organizations, nonprofits and institutions of higher education; for-profits ineligible. Every application except a tribe's must be sponsored by the State Forester (CAL FIRE in California); draft narrative and budget are due to the State Forester by December 17, 2026, and each State Forester may sponsor up to 10 projects (5 single-state, 5 multistate). Work must be on rural non-industrial private or rural state and local forest land (outside Census places over 50,000); urban or federal-land work disqualifies the project. Tribes are limited to two applications under this notice.
grants.Deadline: January 26, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern via Grants.gov; awards anticipated spring 2027.
grants.Program Focus: Competitive, science-based restoration of priority non-federal forest landscapes: wildfire risk reduction, watershed and water-quality protection, habitat, and insect, disease and invasive-species response, with measurable outcomes and leverage. This is the standing LSR round, and the State Forester gate makes mid-December the real deadline: counties, RCDs, land trusts, fire safe councils, tribes and university extension programs that want a CAL FIRE sponsorship slot need a project concept and partner list by early December. Multistate projects (for example along the Oregon–California border or across tribal lands in Arizona and New Mexico) unlock the $600,000 ceiling. Good material for a short outreach campaign to forestry, fire and watershed contacts.
grants.Cost Share / Match: 1:1 non-federal match required (cash or in-kind); territories and Freely Associated States are exempt for grants of $500,000 or less.
grants.Primary Sector: Natural Resources; Wildfire Prevention; Restoration; Water; State & Local Government; Tribal Programs
grants.Link to NOFO: Listing on Simpler.Grants.gov; NOFO (PDF, October 27, 2026); Forest Service LSR program page

grants.Description: NOAA Climate Program Office — FY2027 Super Intelligence/Machine Learning Innovation to Advance Earth System Science and Support Hazard Resilience
grants.Agency / Funder: NOAA Oceanic and Atmospheric Research, Climate Program Office (MAPP, AdSci and NIHHIS programs). Competition manager Kathleen Palermo, Kathleen.Palermo@noaa.gov; MAPP Daniel Barrie, Daniel.Barrie@noaa.gov; AdSci Bhaskar Subramanian, Bhaskar.Subramanian@noaa.gov; NIHHIS Barbara Boustead, barbara.boustead@noaa.gov.
grants.Total Funding: Not specified in the NOFO; CPO "may fund up to 15 new awards".
grants.Award Range: Most awards up to $250,000 per year for one to three years (listing ceiling $750,000; the listing's $1 floor is a placeholder).
grants.Eligible Applicants: Institutions of higher education, other nonprofits, commercial organizations, local and federally recognized tribal governments, and federal agencies with transfer authority. Foreign institutions are not eligible; state governments are not listed (a state agency should confirm eligibility with the competition manager before investing effort).
grants.Deadline: Letters of intent encouraged by November 17, 2026, 11:59 p.m. Pacific (not required); full applications February 9, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Pacific.
grants.Program Focus: AI and machine-learning research in three areas: multi-year to decadal climate prediction and model emulation; social-science study of how AI tools inform hazard-resilience decisions, with stated interest in small and mid-size communities; and extreme-heat thresholds, impacts on health, infrastructure and agriculture, and forecast skill. Fits university climate and data-science groups, resilience nonprofits and consultancies, and local or tribal governments partnering as decision-maker case studies. The Pacific-time deadlines and November LOI make this a quick university outreach item; note the government-wide relabeling of AI as "Super Intelligence" in NOAA and NSF titles.
grants.Primary Sector: Climate and Atmospheric Research; Research & Development; Hazard Mitigation; Science

grants.Description: DOJ Bureau of Justice Assistance — FY2026 Postconviction Testing of DNA Evidence
grants.Agency / Funder: DOJ Office of Justice Programs, Bureau of Justice Assistance. OJP Response Center, OJP.ResponseCenter@usdoj.gov, 800-851-3420.
grants.Total Funding: Up to $11,179,802; 14 awards (12 in Category 1 case review and testing, 2 in Category 2 evidence preservation and records); 36-month projects starting January 1, 2027.
grants.Award Range: Up to $1,000,000 per award (the listing shows $1,000,000 as a minimum; the NOFO gives it as the maximum).
grants.Eligible Applicants: State governments, county, city and township governments, special districts, other units of local government, and public and state-controlled institutions of higher education. State and local applicants must submit the chief-executive certification (Appendix 1) or be denied; a certification on postconviction DNA testing and preservation of biological evidence from the state's chief legal officer is required before funds flow; an 8 U.S.C. 1373 compliance condition is expected.
grants.Deadline: Grants.gov SF-424 December 8, 2026, 11:59 p.m. Eastern; JustGrants full application December 15, 2026, 8:59 p.m. Eastern.
grants.Program Focus: Funds postconviction case review, location of biological evidence and DNA testing in violent-felony cases where testing could show actual innocence, plus modernization of evidence-preservation systems and records. Natural applicants are state attorney general offices, public defender and conviction-integrity units inside state or local government, state crime labs, and public universities hosting innocence projects (a path for university clients). Priority consideration goes to applications that support law enforcement operations, including immigration enforcement, which some jurisdictions will weigh against the certification.
grants.Primary Sector: Law Enforcement; Public Safety; State & Local Government; Education

grants.Description: AFRL/AFOSR — FY2027 University Center for High-Speed Aerothermoelasticity
grants.Agency / Funder: Air Force Research Laboratory / Air Force Office of Scientific Research, with the AFRL Air Warfare Directorate. Program officer Dr. Amanda Chou, aerothermodynamics@us.af.mil (put the NOFO number in the subject line); grants officer Shelby Bonneville, shelby.bonneville@us.af.mil.
grants.Total Funding: $13,750,000 over five years if options are exercised (base $8,250,000 over three years); one award.
grants.Award Range: Up to $2,750,000 per year; of that, $750,000 per year is available only if the team includes three investigators with full-time appointments at an HBCU (no single HBCU investigator above $250,000 per year). Section D.4.g of the NOFO also says "the budget may not exceed $150,000 annually", which conflicts with the rest of the document — confirm with the program officer.
grants.Eligible Applicants: U.S. public, state and private institutions of higher education only; the PI must be a full-time permanent or tenure-track faculty member and a U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident; FFRDCs and Department of War laboratories are ineligible; up to ten investigators.

grants.Description: Interior and seven agencies — Proposed Extension of the Build America, Buy America Manufactured-Products Waiver for Indian Tribes
grants.Issuing Agency: Department of the Interior (lead) with USDA, Education, DOE, HUD, EPA, FEMA and Commerce
grants.Effective Date: Published October 23, 2026; comments due November 23, 2026; if finalized, the waiver runs through December 31, 2026.
grants.Summary: Proposes extending the manufactured-products element of the January 10, 2025 general-applicability public-interest BABA waiver for federal financial assistance to Indian tribes through the end of 2026 while the agencies study longer-term changes. It would cover funds obligated on or after the final waiver's effective date and unexpended funds under earlier awards. The agencies ask for input on critical manufactured products, the availability of BABA-compliant vendors including Native enterprises, and domestic supply.
grants.Who It Affects: Tribal governments and tribal entities holding IIJA and other infrastructure awards from the eight agencies (water, energy, broadband, housing, transportation).
grants.GMA Action Items: Tribal clients should time obligations and procurements to the waiver window, submit comments by November 23 documenting product-availability gaps, and plan for full BABA compliance after December 31, 2026 absent a further extension.

grants.Description: HHS Administration for Children and Families — Proposed Rule: Reducing Bureaucracy and Burden for Block Grants (45 CFR Part 96)
grants.Issuing Agency: HHS Administration for Children and Families
grants.Summary: Proposes removing obsolete and several substantive provisions of the block-grant rules that govern CSBG, SSBG, LIHEAP, the mental-health and substance-use block grants, Preventive Health and MCH: it deletes the SSBG definitions and Appendix A service definitions, the CSBG scope and audit sections and most of the LIHEAP weatherization limits (the good-cause waiver stays), rewrites the waiver-request routing and updates obligation and expenditure periods (adding two-year limits for MHBG and SUBG). HHS labels the rule significant and conducted no tribal consultation.
grants.Who It Affects: State, territorial and tribal block-grant grantees; community action agencies; LIHEAP weatherization subgrantees; county human-services departments.
grants.GMA Action Items: Review with clients that administer or subcontract under these block grants; consider comments by November 30, especially on weatherization flexibility and the loss of the CSBG audit provisions; update compliance checklists if the rule is finalized.

grants.Description: White House — Proclamation Adjusting Imports of Robotics, Industrial Machinery, and Their Parts and Components (Section 232)
grants.Reference #: Presidential proclamation signed October 28, 2026; Federal Register citation pending – needs verification at source
grants.Issuing Agency: Executive Office of the President (Commerce Section 232 investigation)
grants.Effective Date: Signed October 28, 2026; no tariff imposed; Commerce and USTR report due within 180 days (about April 26, 2027).
grants.Summary: Following Commerce's finding that imports of robotics, industrial machinery and their parts threaten national security, the President imposed no new tariff but directed Commerce and USTR to negotiate with trading partners and report within 180 days, after which tariffs, quotas, fees or "a program to incentivize new investment in United States production" may follow. It mirrors the October 22 wind-turbine proclamation (now published at 91 FR 68001, Proclamation 11074). No HTS codes, countries or exclusion process are listed.
grants.Who It Affects: Advanced and automation-dependent manufacturers, defense industrial-base suppliers, and community colleges and workforce programs buying robotics and training equipment with grant funds.
grants.GMA Action Items: Document equipment sourcing and cost assumptions in FY2027 proposals and budgets; flag tariff contingency for equipment-heavy projects; watch for a domestic-investment incentive program as a future funding vehicle for manufacturing clients.

grants.Description: Nuclear Regulatory Commission — Final Rule: NRC Reviews of Reactor Designs Previously Authorized by DOE or the Department of War
grants.Summary: Adds 10 CFR 50.43(f) and revises 10 CFR 53.440(a)(1) so commercial reactor applicants can rely on information from a prior DOE or Department of War demonstration-reactor authorization to demonstrate safety functions; applicants map that information to NRC requirements and fill gaps, and NRC retains independent review. Implements section 5(d) of Executive Order 14300.
grants.Who It Affects: Advanced reactor developers, including DOE Reactor Pilot Program participants; utilities and public power; universities and national laboratories partnering on demonstrations.
grants.GMA Action Items: Cite the expedited pathway in nuclear proposals and commercialization plans; align DOE demonstration-award narratives with eventual NRC licensing; pair with the DOE Energy Dominance Financing nuclear pipeline below.

grants.Description: DOE Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation — Critical Material List: Addition of Helium
grants.Effective Date: Published October 27, 2026 (signed October 21; DOE release October 23); no effective date stated.
grants.Summary: DOE adds helium to its Critical Material List under section 7002(a)(2) of the Energy Act of 2020, citing semiconductor manufacturing, gas-infrastructure leak testing, quantum computing and the AI Action Plan. The notice does not reference specific DOE programs or tax provisions.
grants.Who It Affects: Helium producers and recyclers, semiconductor and gas-processing projects, and applicants to DOE critical-materials programs whose eligibility keys off the list.
grants.GMA Action Items: Ask tax counsel and the CMEI program office whether the section 48C "critical materials" definition and current critical-materials NOFOs now reach helium projects; the statutory 45X applicable-critical-minerals list is unchanged.

grants.Description: EPA — Proposed Rule: Alaska Underground Injection Control Program, Class VI Primacy
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Water
grants.Effective Date: Published October 29, 2026; comments due December 14, 2026; one virtual hearing, date to be posted.
grants.Summary: Proposes approving the Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission's primacy for Class VI geologic-sequestration wells (excluding Indian country and exclusive federal jurisdiction), the third Class VI primacy action this month after Colorado (effective November 12) and Utah (proposed; comments December 7). EPA retains oversight through quarterly noncompliance and annual reports.
grants.Who It Affects: Carbon capture and storage developers, oil and gas and LNG operators in Alaska, and 45Q tax-credit strategies.
grants.GMA Action Items: For Alaska CCS clients, model faster state permitting timelines in project schedules and DOE applications; comment by December 14 if the Indian-country exclusion matters to a tribal client.

grants.Description: EPA — Proposed Rule: Additional Reconsideration of Oil and Natural Gas NSPS OOOOb and Emission Guidelines OOOOc
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Air and Radiation
grants.Effective Date: Published October 29, 2026; comments due December 16, 2026; virtual hearing November 13 or 16 (the document is inconsistent), speaker registration by November 10.
grants.Summary: Proposes rescinding the Super Emitter Program across the OOOO rules, creating well-site subcategories (marginal versus non-marginal, or conventional versus non-conventional) with reduced requirements for the lower-burden group, and revising associated-gas, liquids-unloading, controller, pump, fugitive-emissions, storage-vessel and control-device monitoring provisions, with Appendix K optical gas imaging allowed at gas plants.
grants.Who It Affects: Oil and gas operators, states preparing OOOOc plans, methane-mitigation technology vendors, and the value case for methane-reduction grant projects.
grants.GMA Action Items: Advise energy clients on reduced compliance drivers; adjust the cost-avoidance arguments in methane-reduction and gas-infrastructure grant applications; track the hearing date correction.

grants.Description: OMB and OPM — Memorandum M-27-01: Status of Documents Addressing Reductions in Force During a Lapse in Appropriations
grants.Issuing Agency: Office of Management and Budget and Office of Personnel Management
grants.Summary: Under the settlement in AFGE v. OMB, rescinds in full OMB's September 24, 2025 lapse email and OPM's 2025 shutdown-furlough guidance that authorized reduction-in-force activity during a lapse. It says nothing about grants, but it is active shutdown housekeeping five weeks before the continuing resolution expires on December 11, 2026; Congress was in pre-election recess with no appropriations action in the window, and CR section 157 still blocks OMB from finalizing the 2 CFR 200 rewrite until then.
grants.Who It Affects: All federal grantees and applicants with December and January deadlines; agencies' ability to process awards, drawdowns and extensions during a lapse.
grants.GMA Action Items: Refresh client lapse playbooks before December 11 (drawdown timing, agency contact availability, expectations for deadline extensions) and prepare for a 2 CFR 200 final rule or another CR block in the lame-duck session.

grants.Description: Bureau of Land Management — Termination of the Programmatic EIS and Resource Management Plan Amendments for Section 368 Energy Corridor Revisions
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Land Management
grants.Summary: BLM ends the programmatic EIS begun in December 2023 to revise the West-wide Section 368 energy corridors, saying updated processing methods and tools allow linear energy infrastructure to be sited without it; no replacement process is described.
grants.Who It Affects: Transmission developers, pipeline sponsors, utilities and public power siting across BLM land in the western states; DOE grid-program applicants whose timelines assumed corridor updates.
grants.GMA Action Items: For western transmission and pipeline projects, plan project-specific NEPA and right-of-way strategies and adjust schedule risk in DOE and state applications.

grants.Description: DOE Office of Energy Dominance Financing — $5 Billion Nuclear Uprate Commitment and $5.1 Billion Utility Loan Close; eXCHANGE Portals Consolidated
grants.Reference #: DOE announcements October 26–28, 2026 (no Federal Register citation)
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Energy Dominance Financing (formerly the Loan Programs Office)
grants.Effective Date: Constellation conditional commitment announced October 27; Alliant Energy financial close October 28, 2026.
grants.Summary: DOE offered Constellation a conditional commitment of up to $5,000,000,000 for about 1.1 GW of nuclear uprates and modernization at eight plants in Illinois, Maryland and Pennsylvania, with an option to finance future uprates, and closed a $5,100,000,000 loan to Alliant Energy for more than 2.6 GW of gas generation, storage and upgrades in Iowa and Wisconsin — the administration's tenth financial close. DOE's Project UPRISE fact sheet also cites a Vistra commitment of up to $4.2 billion and a $17.5 billion nuclear supply-chain conditional commitment. Separately, DOE consolidated all eXCHANGE application portals (EERE, OCED, Indian Energy, Infrastructure, ARPA-E) into exchange.energy.gov in October; the old URLs show decommission notices and the site carries a court-ordered restraining-order banner.
grants.Who It Affects: Utilities, cooperatives and public power, nuclear supply-chain firms, developers of gas, storage and grid projects; every DOE grant applicant who must re-register on the consolidated portal.
grants.GMA Action Items: Position utility and public-power clients for EDF pre-application consultations (uprates, restarts, gas, storage, grid) and stack with 45U, 45Y and 48E where applicable (tax counsel); have DOE applicants confirm their accounts and pending submissions on exchange.energy.gov before November deadlines.

grants.Description: EPA — PFAS TECH Strategy Launched; FY2026 "Reducing Lead Where Children Learn" Allotments Announced
grants.Reference #: EPA announcements October 26 and 29, 2026 (no Federal Register citation)
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Water and Office of Research and Development
grants.Effective Date: Strategy released October 26, 2026; lead-reduction allotments announced October 29, 2026.
grants.Summary: EPA's first PFAS TECH strategy says the agency intends to issue PFAS-destruction research grants through STAR and SBIR (no amounts or dates), run pilot-scale projects at Superfund sites, military facilities, wastewater plants and drinking-water systems, pursue public-private R&D partnerships through the Office of Water and publish a "Break the Bond Navigator" tool. On October 29 EPA announced $26,000,000 in FY2026 WIIN Act section 2107 allotments to 50 states, D.C. and four territories for lead testing and reduction in schools and child-care facilities (formula; tribal allotments to follow; no application deadline — states coordinate with their EPA region).
grants.Who It Affects: Water and wastewater utilities (pilot hosts), universities (STAR), small technology firms (SBIR); state drinking-water programs and the school districts and child-care providers that receive state subgrants.
grants.GMA Action Items: Water-utility clients with PFAS-impacted sources should signal pilot-host interest to EPA Region 9 and the Office of Water; university clients watch for the STAR RFA; school districts ask their state drinking-water program about the lead-reduction subgrant round. The Master Calendar already carries a PFAS TECH watch row (added October 29).
